comment: Shared by the Android JVM tests and the iOS XCTests (FailedLoadRule), and by the Android crossfade orchestrator tests. Chosen alignment (iOS crossfade's loadIndex): a track becomes the active one once it loaded; when a load fails (a give-up at stallTimeoutMs or the total limit, or a player error) the previous track stays active (none when there was none) and the error is reported; the next play loads that previous track. Items are named; 'load' moves the player to an item, 'ready' is the item ready (playing or with media), 'fail' its load failing, 'play' the next play. Each step gives the active item expected after it (null: none), 'revert' the active-track change a standard player reports back to the previous track (null: none) and, for 'play', the item it loads ('reload', null: none, it plays the current one).

scenarios.id: LOAD-01 a skip whose load fails keeps the previous track, and play reloads it
LOAD-02 a load that succeeds makes its track active
LOAD-03 a first load that fails leaves no active track
LOAD-04 an error on a track that had loaded keeps it active (no revert)
LOAD-05 a retry that fails again keeps the previous track
